title.narrative: Power Africa: Nigeria Power Sector Program (NPSP)

description.narrative: (USAID Africa Regional): The Nigeria Power Sector Program (NPSP) seeks comprehensive reform within Nigeria's power sector. USAID AFR Regional FY 2022 funds will support this activity to address gas-to-power challenges; competitive procurement of clean and conventional energy; regulatory and policy reforms; utility distribution sector reform; and off-grid electricity access...To achieve its goals of 10,000 megawatts (MW) and three million new connections to homes and businesses by 2023, NPSP will: 1) continue to provide senior technical advisors to the core Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN) beneficiary ministries; 2) provide trainings to the FGN, its agencies, ministries and the private sector; and 3) convene local counterparts to advance policies and build capacity in the electricity supply industry...NPSP will seek to reduce greenhouse emissions by supporting clean energy and flare gas capturing projects. Captured flares will be commercialized for power generation, reducing electricity generation demand from inefficient off-grid, diesel/petrol-fired generators. NPSP will also continue to increase grid capacity, reduce technical losses and enhance operational performance of distribution utilities. This will reduce compensatory generation leading to additional greenhouse gas emissions...NPSP will continue work with the FGN to establish and implement policies that give local and foreign private sector companies, including American companies, a fair chance at competing. Calls for tenders and other opportunities will be disseminated to Power Africa partners and U.S. companies...NPSP will also continue to assist the private sector by building models and providing analysis that increases access to financing...Finally, NPSP will continue to foster enhanced roles for women in power sector institutions by promoting skill development, better hiring practices, increased access to finance for female entrepreneurs, and policy reforms to incorporate gender into energy planning
